Fig. 4: Controller architecture. The controller takes LLM hidden states h(ℓ)t and the current option ω (ℓ) t−1 (a set of k̂ expert indices) as inputs. A DeepSets encoder maps ω (ℓ) t−1 to a permutation-invariant set embedding z, which is concatenated with h(ℓ)t (after RMSNorm) and fed to the termination head βω and the selection head. The state-value head VΩ uses h(ℓ)t alone. The selection head is a linear layer initialized from the router weights and produces candidate logits c(ℓ)t = fsel(h (ℓ) t ), from which k̂ experts are sampled via the Plackett–Luce distribution. If the Bernoulli sample d(ℓ)t =1, the newly sampled option replaces the current one; otherwise the current option persists.
